entry_1.statement: A subset $S \subseteq V$ \textbf{spans} $V$ if every $v \in V$ can be expressed as a finite sum $v = \sum_i \lambda_i s_i$ with $\lambda_i \in F$, $s_i \in S$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field and $M$ is a left $R$-module. The smallest $R$-submodule of $M$ containing $S$ is all of $M$ precisely when no proper $R$-submodule contains $S$.

entry_1.statement: A subset $B \subseteq V$ is a \textbf{basis} if every $v \in V$ has a unique finite representation $v = \sum_i \lambda_i b_i$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. A family $B \subseteq M$ exhibits $M$ as the coproduct of copies of $R$ indexed by $B$, i.e. the canonical map \[  igoplus_{b \in B} R 	o M \] sending the $b$th coordinate vector to $b$ is an isomorphism.

entry_1.statement: $W \subseteq V$ is a \textbf{subspace} if $0 \in W$, $W$ is closed under addition, and $\lambda w \in W$ for all $\lambda \in F$, $w \in W$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. A nonempty subset $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is an $R$-submodule exactly when the restriction of the ambient addition and scalar action turns $N$ into an $R$-module and the inclusion $N \hookrightarrow M$ is $R$-linear.

entry_1.statement: A map $T : V \to W$ is \textbf{linear} if $T(u+v) = T(u) + T(v)$ and $T(\lambda v) = \lambda T(v)$ for $\lambda \in F$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. A function $\varphi:M\to N$ is a morphism of left $R$-modules when it commutes with the module structures: it preserves the abelian-group operation and the action map of $R$.

entry_1.statement: For a linear map $T : V \to W$, $\ker T = \{v \in V : T(v) = 0\}$ is a subspace of $V$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For any morphism $\varphi:M\to N$ of $R$-modules, the fiber over the zero element of $N$ is closed under the inherited module operations.

entry_1.statement: For linear $T : V \to W$, the induced map $V / \ker T \to \operatorname{im} T$ is an isomorphism of vector spaces.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. Any $R$-module morphism $\varphi:M\to N$ passes through the quotient of $M$ by the fiber over zero, and the resulting middle comparison identifies that quotient bijectively with the image submodule.

entry_1.statement: For a subspace $W \subseteq V$, the set of cosets $V/W$ inherits a vector space structure via $[v] + [v'] = [v+v']$, $\lambda[v] = [\lambda v]$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field and $N$ is an $R$-submodule of $M$. The abelian quotient $M/N$ admits exactly one compatible $R$-module structure for which the canonical projection is $R$-linear.

entry_1.statement: $V = U \oplus W$ iff $V = U + W$ and $U \cap W = \{0\}$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. The addition map $N_1 \times N_2 \to M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules exactly when every element of $M$ decomposes in one and only one way using one element from each $N_i$.

entry_1.statement: Any two bases of a vector space have the same cardinality.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. If $M \cong \bigoplus_{i\in I} R \cong \bigoplus_{j\in J} R$, then the indexing sets $I$ and $J$ have the same cardinality.

pairs.topic: Dual space / Hom into the ground

entry_1.statement: The \textbf{dual} of $V$ is $V^* = \{f : V \to F \mid f \text{ is linear}\}$, itself a vector space.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. The contravariant representable functor obtained by mapping an $R$-module $M$ to its scalar-valued $R$-linear morphisms is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$, equipped with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.

entry_1.statement: A \textbf{bilinear form} on $V$ is a map $B : V \times V \to F$ that is linear in each slot.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. A scalar-valued two-argument operation on an $R$-module $M$ is $R$-bilinear exactly when, after either input is fixed, the remaining one-variable map lies in $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$.

entry_1.statement: The tensor product $V \otimes_F W$ is the vector space such that bilinear maps $V \times W \to U$ correspond naturally to linear maps $V \otimes_F W \to U$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. There is an $R$-module equipped with a universal two-variable $R$-linear map out of $M\times N$; composing with that universal map identifies maps from this module to any target $P$ with such two-variable maps into $P$.

entry_1.statement: For linear $T : V \to W$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, $\dim V = \dim \ker T + \dim \operatorname{im} T$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For an $R$-linear morphism $\varphi:M\to N$ with $M$ of finite rank, the short exact sequence $0\to\ker\varphi\to M\to\varphi(M)\to0$ gives additivity of rank across its three nonzero terms.

pairs.topic: Sum of subspaces is a subspace

entry_1.statement: For subspaces $U, W \subseteq V$, the set $U + W = \{u + w : u \in U,\ w \in W\}$ is itself a subspace.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For two subobjects $A,B\subseteq M$ in $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, the image of the addition morphism $A\oplus B\to M$ is again an object of the same submodule lattice.

entry_1.statement: For a subspace $W \subseteq V$, $W^\circ = \{f \in V^* : f(W) = 0\}$ is a subspace of $V^*$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For an inclusion $N\hookrightarrow M$, the zero fiber of the restriction map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)$ is closed under the inherited pointwise $R$-module operations.

entry_1.statement: Every vector space admits a basis.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. Every object of $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of the one-dimensional module $R$.

entry_1.statement: Given a basis $B$ of $V$ and any function $f : B \to W$, there is a unique linear extension $\tilde f : V \to W$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For $L=\bigoplus_{b\in B} R$, restriction to the distinguished summand generators gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,N)\cong\operatorname{Map}(B,N)$.

entry_1.statement: An $n$-dimensional vector space over $F$ is isomorphic to $F^n$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. Any finitely generated object of $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is classified, up to isomorphism, by a natural number $n$ and is represented by the $n$-fold product of the scalar module.

entry_1.statement: The set of linear maps $V \to V$ forms an associative $F$-algebra under composition.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. The self-morphisms of an $R$-module $M$ can be added pointwise and chained, with the identity map as unit; these operations make them the usual endomorphism ring over $R$.

entry_1.statement: A subspace $W \subseteq V$ is \textbf{invariant} under $T : V \to V$ if $T(W) \subseteq W$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. If an endomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$ is regarded as the action of an indeterminate, the $R$-submodules preserved by that action are precisely the submodules on which $\varphi$ restricts to an endomorphism.

entry_1.statement: An endomorphism $P : V \to V$ satisfying $P^2 = P$ induces $V = \ker P \oplus \operatorname{im} P$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. If $e$ is an idempotent self-morphism of an $R$-module $M$, then the maps $e$ and $1-e$ exhibit $M$ as the biproduct of the two corresponding retracts.

entry_1.statement: Every subspace $W \subseteq V$ has a complementary subspace $U$ with $V = W \oplus U$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. For any monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow M$ in $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, there exists another object $B$ for which the induced map $A\oplus B\to M$ is an isomorphism.

pairs.topic: Linear maps determined on a basis

entry_1.statement: A linear map out of $V$ is uniquely determined by its values on any basis of $V$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. When $L$ is presented as $\bigoplus_{b\in B}R$, two arrows $L\to N$ in $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ are equal once they agree on the canonical elements indexed by $B$.

entry_1.statement: Given a basis $(e_1, \dots, e_n)$ of $V$, there exist $f_1, \dots, f_n \in V^*$ with $f_i(e_j) = \delta_{ij}$, forming a basis of $V^*$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. If $M\cong R^n$ is specified by ordered generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, evaluation at these generators identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with $R^n$; under this identification, the standard coordinate functionals give the corresponding free generators.

entry_1.statement: Every surjective linear map $T : V \to W$ has a right inverse, i.e., a linear $s : W \to V$ with $T \circ s = \mathrm{id}_W$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. In $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, every epimorphism admits a section, equivalently each exact row $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ is isomorphic to the row obtained from $A\oplus C$.

pairs.topic: Double dual / Reflexivity in finite dimensions

entry_1.statement: For finite-dimensional $V$, the map $V \to V^{**}$, $v \mapsto (f \mapsto f(v))$, is an isomorphism.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. A finite-rank free $R$-module is recovered canonically from the scalar-valued functionals on its scalar-valued functionals.

entry_1.statement: If $S : U \to V$ and $T : V \to W$ are linear, then $T \circ S$ is linear.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. The objects and arrows of $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ are closed under the categorical operation of chaining composable arrows.

entry_1.statement: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique vector space of dimension zero.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. The zero object of $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is unique up to unique isomorphism, so an $R$-module whose underlying set has only the additive identity has no nontrivial isomorphism type.

entry_1.statement: A bijective linear map between vector spaces has a linear inverse.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. An arrow in $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ whose underlying function is one-to-one and onto automatically has an inverse arrow in the same category.

entry_1.statement: For finite-dimensional $V, W$, $\dim \operatorname{Hom}_F(V, W) = \dim V \cdot \dim W$.

entry_2.statement: Assume $R$ is a field. If $M$ and $N$ have finite ranks $m$ and $n$, then the module of arrows from $M$ to $N$ is coordinatized by an $n\times m$ array of scalars.

entry_1.statement: A probability space is a triple $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ where $\mathcal{F}$ is a $\sigma$-algebra of events on the sample space $\Omega$ and $P$ is a countably additive function $\mathcal{F} \to [0,1]$ with $P(\Omega) = 1$.

entry_2.statement: A normalized measure space is a measure space $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ whose entire underlying set has total measure $1$.

entry_1.statement: A random variable is a map $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\{X \leq a\}$ is an event for every $a \in \mathbb{R}$.

entry_2.statement: A real-valued function on $(X,\Sigma)$ is measurable exactly when pulling back any Borel subset of the real line produces a member of $\Sigma$.

entry_1.statement: The expected value $\mathbb{E}[X]$ of an integrable random variable is its average outcome weighted by likelihood under $P$.

entry_2.statement: On a finite measure space of total mass one, the Lebesgue integral of an $L^1$ function is its barycenter with respect to the underlying measure.

entry_1.statement: The law of a random variable $X$ is the assignment $B \mapsto P(X \in B)$ on Borel sets.

entry_2.statement: Given a measurable map $T$ out of $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$, the transported measure on the target assigns to each measurable target set the $\mu$-mass of its inverse image under $T$.

pairs.topic: Independence / Product factorization of joint law

entry_1.statement: Two random variables $X, Y$ are independent iff $P(X \in A,\, Y \in B) = P(X \in A) \cdot P(Y \in B)$ for all Borel sets $A, B$.

entry_2.statement: For measurable functions $f$ and $g$ on a normalized measure space, independence is equivalently the assertion that the measure transported by the combined map $x\mapsto(f(x),g(x))$ is the tensor product of the two separately transported measures.

entry_1.statement: A statement holds almost surely if the event on which it fails has probability zero.

entry_2.statement: A property holds $\mu$-almost everywhere when, after discarding a measurable set of measure zero, no counterexamples remain.

pairs.topic: Convergence in probability / Convergence in measure

entry_1.statement: $X_n \to X$ in probability if $P(|X_n - X| > \varepsilon) \to 0$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

entry_2.statement: On a finite measure space, convergence in measure means that for every positive tolerance, the region where the error exceeds that tolerance eventually has measure tending to zero.

pairs.topic: Almost sure convergence / Pointwise convergence a.e.

entry_1.statement: $X_n \to X$ almost surely if $P(\{\omega : X_n(\omega) \to X(\omega)\}) = 1$.

entry_2.statement: A sequence of measurable functions converges pointwise $\mu$-almost everywhere precisely when the set of points at which ordinary pointwise convergence fails is negligible.

entry_1.statement: For $p \geq 1$, $X_n \to X$ in $L^p$ iff $\mathbb{E}[|X_n - X|^p] \to 0$.

entry_2.statement: For $p \geq 1$, convergence in the $L^p(\mu)$ metric is equivalent to the $p$th power of the distance, computed by integrating $|f_n-f|^p$, tending to zero.

entry_1.statement: For a nonnegative random variable $X$ and $a > 0$, $P(X \geq a) \leq \mathbb{E}[X] / a$.

entry_2.statement: For a nonnegative measurable function and any positive threshold, the measure of the region above that threshold is bounded by the total area under the function divided by the threshold.

entry_1.statement: For $X$ with finite variance and $a>0$, $P(|X - \mathbb{E}[X]| \geq a) \leq \mathrm{Var}(X) / a^2$.

entry_2.statement: On a normalized measure space, the region where an $L^2$ function lies at distance at least $t>0$ from its mean has measure at most $t^{-2}$ times the squared $L^2$-length of its centered part.

entry_1.statement: $\mathrm{Var}(X) = \mathbb{E}[(X - \mathbb{E}[X])^2] = \mathbb{E}[X^2] - (\mathbb{E}[X])^2$.

entry_2.statement: On a measure space of total mass one, the squared $L^2$-length of an observable after subtracting its mean equals its second moment minus the square of that mean.

entry_1.statement: A random variable $X$ admits a density $p$ when $P(X \in B) = \int_B p(x)\, dx$ for every Borel set $B$.

entry_2.statement: A finite Borel measure on the real line has no singular part relative to Lebesgue measure precisely when it can be recovered by integrating some $L^1$ function against Lebesgue measure.

entry_1.statement: Given integrable $X$ and a sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{F}$, $\mathbb{E}[X \mid \mathcal{G}]$ is the (a.s. unique) $\mathcal{G}$-measurable $Y$ satisfying $\int_A Y\, dP = \int_A X\, dP$ for every $A \in \mathcal{G}$.

entry_2.statement: Given an $L^1$ function and a smaller $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{T}$, there is a unique $\mu$-a.e. $\mathcal{T}$-measurable representative whose integrals over all $\mathcal{T}$-sets match those of the original function.

entry_1.statement: For convex $\varphi$ and integrable $X$, $\varphi(\mathbb{E}[X]) \leq \mathbb{E}[\varphi(X)]$.

entry_2.statement: On a normalized measure space, applying an upward-curving real function after taking the barycenter of a finite-expectation observable never exceeds averaging the transformed observable, whenever that average is defined.

entry_1.statement: For square-integrable $X, Y$, $(\mathbb{E}[XY])^2 \leq \mathbb{E}[X^2]\, \mathbb{E}[Y^2]$.

entry_2.statement: In the Hilbert space $L^2(\mu)$, the absolute value of the inner product of two elements is bounded by the product of their lengths.

entry_1.statement: If $X_n \to X$ almost surely and $|X_n| \leq Y$ for some integrable $Y$, then $\mathbb{E}[X_n] \to \mathbb{E}[X]$.

entry_2.statement: A pointwise a.e. limit may be passed through the Lebesgue integral when the entire sequence is dominated in absolute value by a single integrable function.

entry_1.statement: If $0 \leq X_n \uparrow X$ almost surely, then $\mathbb{E}[X_n] \uparrow \mathbb{E}[X]$.

entry_2.statement: For a nondecreasing a.e. sequence of nonnegative measurable functions, the integral of the pointwise limit is the increasing limit of the integrals.

entry_1.statement: For nonnegative random variables, $\mathbb{E}[\liminf_n X_n] \leq \liminf_n \mathbb{E}[X_n]$.

entry_2.statement: For nonnegative measurable functions, integrating the lower pointwise limit cannot give a value larger than the lower limit of the individual integrals.

pairs.topic: Independence factorization of expectation / Fubini on a product

entry_1.statement: For independent $X, Y$ and suitable $f, g$, $\mathbb{E}[f(X) g(Y)] = \mathbb{E}[f(X)] \cdot \mathbb{E}[g(Y)]$.

entry_2.statement: For $\sigma$-finite measure spaces and integrable factors $f$ and $g$, the product-measure integral of the separated function $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ factors into the two one-space integrals.

pairs.topic: Characteristic function / Fourier transform of measure

entry_1.statement: The characteristic function of a random variable $X$ is $\varphi_X(t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{itX}]$.

entry_2.statement: A finite Borel measure on the real line determines a complex-valued transform by integrating the oscillatory character $x\mapsto e^{itx}$ against that measure.

pairs.topic: Convergence in distribution / Weak convergence of measures

entry_1.statement: $X_n \to X$ in distribution iff $\mathbb{E}[h(X_n)] \to \mathbb{E}[h(X)]$ for every bounded continuous $h$.

entry_2.statement: A sequence of probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$ tends weakly to a limiting measure exactly when all bounded continuous test functions have convergent integrals against the sequence.

pairs.topic: Tightness of a family of variables / Tightness of laws

entry_1.statement: A family $\{X_\alpha\}$ is tight if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a compact $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $P(X_\alpha \in K) \geq 1 - \varepsilon$ for all $\alpha$.

entry_2.statement: A collection of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$ is tight when, for each allowed loss $\varepsilon>0$, one compact set captures all but less than $\varepsilon$ of every measure in the collection.

entry_1.statement: If $\sum_n P(A_n) < \infty$, then with probability one only finitely many of the events $A_n$ occur.

entry_2.statement: If the measures of a countable list of measurable sets are summable, then the limsup of that list is a null set.

entry_1.statement: Sub-$\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2$ are independent if $P(A \cap B) = P(A) P(B)$ for all $A \in \mathcal{F}_1$, $B \in \mathcal{F}_2$.

entry_2.statement: For two collections of measurable events inside a normalized measure space, independence means that the mass assigned to any intersection of one event from each collection is the product of the two separate masses.

entry_1.statement: For integrable $X$ and $\mathcal{G} \subset \mathcal{H} \subset \mathcal{F}$, $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[X \mid \mathcal{H}] \mid \mathcal{G}] = \mathbb{E}[X \mid \mathcal{G}]$ almost surely.

entry_2.statement: For nested sub-$\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{T}\subset\mathcal{U}\subset\Sigma$, conditioning first onto $\mathcal{U}$ and then onto $\mathcal{T}$ gives the same $L^1$ class as conditioning directly onto $\mathcal{T}$.

entry_1.statement: For $X \in L^p$ and $Y \in L^q$ with conjugate $p,q>1$ and $1/p + 1/q = 1$, $\mathbb{E}[|XY|] \leq (\mathbb{E}[|X|^p])^{1/p} (\mathbb{E}[|Y|^q])^{1/q}$.

entry_2.statement: Multiplication sends an $L^p(\mu)$ element and an $L^q(\mu)$ element, for conjugate exponents, into $L^1(\mu)$ with norm no larger than the product of their two norms.

pairs.topic: Change of variables under a distribution / Pushforward integration

entry_1.statement: For random variable $X$ with law $\mu_X$ and measurable $h$ such that one side is defined, $\mathbb{E}[h(X)] = \int_{\mathbb{R}} h(x)\, d\mu_X(x)$.

entry_2.statement: Transporting a measure along a measurable map preserves integrals in the sense that integrating an admissible target function after transport equals integrating its pullback on the source.

pairs.topic: CDF / Stieltjes function of a measure

entry_1.statement: The cumulative distribution function $F(t) = P(X \leq t)$ is non-decreasing, right-continuous, with $\lim_{t \to -\infty} F(t) = 0$ and $\lim_{t \to \infty} F(t) = 1$.

entry_2.statement: A Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ is encoded uniquely by its half-line masses $(-\infty,t]$; the resulting real function is increasing, right-continuous, and approaches the endpoint values $0$ and $1$ at the two infinities.

entry_1.statement: Every distribution on $\mathbb{R}$ decomposes uniquely as a sum of a part possessing a density and a part concentrated on a set of Lebesgue measure zero.

entry_2.statement: Relative to ordinary length on $\mathbb{R}$, each finite Borel law admits exactly one decomposition into an absolutely continuous summand and a singular summand carried by a length-null set.

entry_1.statement: The product of sets $A, B$ is $A \times B = \{(a, b) : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$, with projections $\pi_1(a,b) = a$, $\pi_2(a,b) = b$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, a product of $A$ and $B$ is a cone over the discrete diagram $A,B$ that is terminal among all such cones: maps into it are uniquely the same as choosing one map into $A$ and one map into $B$.

entry_1.statement: $A \sqcup B = (A \times \{0\}) \cup (B \times \{1\})$, with inclusions $i_1(a) = (a, 0)$, $i_2(b) = (b, 1)$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the coproduct of $A$ and $B$ is an object receiving one arrow from each input and initial with that property: a map out of it is uniquely specified by maps separately out of $A$ and out of $B$.

entry_1.statement: $B^A = \{f : A \to B\}$, the set of all functions from $A$ to $B$, with evaluation $\mathrm{ev}(f, a) = f(a)$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the exponential object $B^A$ represents the functor $C\mapsto \operatorname{Hom}(C\times A,B)$; its counit is the evaluation morphism.

entry_1.statement: A set with exactly one element, say $\{*\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, a terminal object is one at which every hom-set into it has exactly one member.

entry_1.statement: The set $\emptyset$, containing no elements.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, an initial object is one from which each hom-set to another object has exactly one member.

pairs.topic: Element / Generalized element from the point

entry_1.statement: An element $a \in A$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, choosing a member of $A$ is the same as giving a global point, namely a morphism from any terminal object into $A$.

pairs.topic: Subset / Equalizer of characteristic and constant

entry_1.statement: A subset $S \subseteq A$ is determined by its characteristic function $\chi_S : A \to \{0, 1\}$ with $\chi_S(a) = 1$ iff $a \in S$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the inclusion associated to a predicate on $A$ is recovered as the universal subobject on which that predicate agrees with the truth value.

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to B$, $\mathrm{im}(f) = \{f(a) : a \in A\} \subseteq B$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, each morphism admits a canonical factorization through the subobject of its codomain consisting exactly of attained values; the epi part and mono part are determined up to unique isomorphism.

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to B$ and $S \subseteq B$, $f^{-1}(S) = \{a \in A : f(a) \in S\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, base-changing a subobject of $B$ along a map into $B$ yields the subobject of the domain consisting of precisely those points whose image lands in the original subobject.

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to C$ and $g : B \to C$, $A \times_C B = \{(a, b) \in A \times B : f(a) = g(b)\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, a pullback of $A\to C\leftarrow B$ is the limiting cone over that cospan: any other cone with the same commutative comparison factors through it uniquely.

entry_1.statement: For injections $C \hookrightarrow A$ and $C \hookrightarrow B$, the pushout is $(A \sqcup B) / \sim$ where elements of $C$ are identified along the two inclusions.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, gluing $A$ and $B$ along their common copy of $C$ is described by an initial cocone out of the span $A\leftarrow C\to B$: every other compatible pair of maps from $A$ and $B$ factors through it uniquely.

pairs.topic: Equivalence relation / Coequalizer of two maps

entry_1.statement: An equivalence relation on $A$ is a subset $R \subseteq A \times A$ that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive; the quotient $A/R$ identifies elements related by $R$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, collapsing exactly the pairs in an equivalence relation is the universal arrow out of $A$ on which the two structure maps $R\rightrightarrows A$ become indistinguishable.

entry_1.statement: For $f, g : A \to B$, $\{a \in A : f(a) = g(a)\} \subseteq A$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the equalizer of two parallel arrows into $B$ is the largest subobject of their common domain on which the two arrows agree, characterized by unique factorization of every such test subobject.

entry_1.statement: For a set $A$, $\mathrm{id}_A : A \to A$ defined by $\mathrm{id}_A(a) = a$.

entry_2.statement: For each object, category theory singles out a self-arrow that leaves every composable arrow unchanged when inserted on either side.

pairs.topic: Composition of functions / Composition in a category

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to B$, $g : B \to C$, $(g \circ f)(a) = g(f(a))$.

entry_2.statement: In any category, whenever the target of one arrow matches the source of another, there is a prescribed composite; this operation is associative and respects the identity arrows.

entry_1.statement: A function $f : A \to B$ that is both injective and surjective.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, an isomorphism is precisely a morphism that has a two-sided inverse morphism.

entry_1.statement: A function $f : A \to B$ such that $f(a) = f(a') \Rightarrow a = a'$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, a monomorphism is an arrow that remains cancellable from the left: no two maps into its domain become equal after postcomposition with it.

entry_1.statement: A function $f : A \to B$ such that every $b \in B$ has some $a$ with $f(a) = b$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, an epimorphism is an arrow that remains cancellable from the right: no two maps out of its codomain agree after precomposition with it unless they already agree.

entry_1.statement: $\mathcal{P}(A) = \{S : S \subseteq A\}$, in bijection with the set of functions $A \to \{0, 1\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the truth-value object classifies subobjects: each predicate-valued map on $A$ determines, by pulling back truth, exactly one subset of $A$, and every subset arises this way.

pairs.topic: Empty product / Terminal as nullary product

entry_1.statement: The product of zero sets is a one-element set.

entry_2.statement: A nullary product is just a terminal object, since a cone over an empty diagram has no legs and terminality supplies the unique comparison map.

pairs.topic: Empty sum / Initial as nullary coproduct

entry_1.statement: The disjoint union of zero sets is the empty set.

entry_2.statement: A nullary coproduct is just an initial object, since a cocone under an empty diagram has no structure and initiality supplies the unique comparison map.

entry_1.statement: For $\{A_i\}_{i \in I}$, $\prod_{i \in I} A_i = \{f : I \to \bigcup_i A_i \mid f(i) \in A_i\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the product of an indexed family is the terminal way to choose compatible projections to all $A_i$: a map into it is uniquely the same as an $I$-indexed family of maps into the separate factors.

entry_1.statement: For $\{A_i\}_{i \in I}$, $\coprod_i A_i = \{(i, a) : i \in I,\ a \in A_i\}$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the coproduct of an indexed family is the initial way to receive maps from all $A_i$: a map out of it is uniquely the same as an $I$-indexed family of maps out of the separate summands.

pairs.topic: Quotient by a function / Coequalizer with kernel pair

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to B$, the relation $a \sim a' \iff f(a) = f(a')$ partitions $A$, and $A/\!\sim$ is in bijection with $\mathrm{im}(f)$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, identifying exactly those elements of $A$ that a map $f$ sends to the same value gives the coequalizer of its kernel-pair projections; the resulting quotient is canonically the attained-value subset of the codomain.

pairs.topic: Inclusion as a constraint / Subobject as monic up to iso

entry_1.statement: Two subsets $S, S' \subseteq A$ are the same subset iff $S = S'$ as sets of elements.

entry_2.statement: Two monomorphisms with codomain $A$ describe one subobject precisely when they are mutually comparable in the slice over $A$, equivalently when they differ only by an isomorphism over $A$.

entry_1.statement: Functions $A \times B \to C$ correspond bijectively to functions $A \to C^B$ via $f \leftrightarrow (a \mapsto (b \mapsto f(a, b)))$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, exponentiation by $B$ is right adjoint to taking product with $B$, so maps out of $A\times B$ into $C$ are naturally the same as maps out of $A$ into the exponential object.

pairs.topic: Graph of a function / Equalizer with projection

entry_1.statement: For $f : A \to B$, $\Gamma_f = \{(a, f(a)) : a \in A\} \subseteq A \times B$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, the graph of a function is the subobject of $A\times B$ selected by equalizing the two ways of producing a $B$-value: applying the function to the first coordinate or reading the second coordinate.

pairs.topic: Constant function / Factorization through the terminal

entry_1.statement: A function $f : A \to B$ is constant if there is $b \in B$ with $f(a) = b$ for all $a$.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, a map is constant exactly when it passes through a terminal object before reaching its codomain.

pairs.topic: Two-element set / Coproduct of two terminals

entry_1.statement: The set $\{0, 1\}$ has two elements.

entry_2.statement: In \textbf{Set}, taking the coproduct of two terminal objects yields an object with exactly two global points.

pairs.topic: Cardinality preserved by bijection / Iso induces bijection on Hom

entry_1.statement: If $A \cong B$ as sets, then $|A| = |B|$.

entry_2.statement: An isomorphism in \textbf{Set} gives, by postcomposition, a one-to-one correspondence between $X$-indexed generalized elements of its source and of its target for every test set $X$.

entry_1.statement: An affine variety over $k$ is the common vanishing locus of a collection of polynomials in $k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.

entry_2.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, the coordinate algebra attached to an affine algebraic set is a finitely generated reduced $k$-algebra, equivalently a polynomial algebra modulo a radical ideal.

entry_1.statement: A point of an affine variety $V$ over an algebraically closed field.

entry_2.statement: By the weak Nullstellensatz, a closed point of $V$ is encoded algebraically by a maximal ideal in its coordinate algebra $k[V]$.

entry_1.statement: A closed subvariety $W \subseteq V$ is cut out by polynomial equations on $V$.

entry_2.statement: Inside the coordinate algebra, closed subspaces of $V$ are recorded by ideals equal to their own radical, with larger geometric pieces corresponding to smaller such ideals.

pairs.topic: Irreducibility / Primality of the zero ideal

entry_1.statement: A variety is irreducible iff it is not the union of two proper closed subvarieties.

entry_2.statement: For an affine variety with coordinate algebra $k[V]$, geometric irreducibility is equivalent to the zero ideal of $k[V]$ being prime, or equivalently to $k[V]$ being an integral domain.

entry_1.statement: The common vanishing of two systems of equations is the variety on which both systems vanish.

entry_2.statement: In the affine coordinate ring, imposing two collections of equations simultaneously corresponds to passing to the ideal generated by both collections.

entry_1.statement: The locus where at least one of two systems of equations holds is the union of their varieties.

entry_2.statement: In affine space, the closed set obtained by allowing either of two equation systems is represented algebraically by the product of the corresponding ideals, or equivalently by their intersection after taking radicals.

entry_1.statement: Polynomials $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ over an algebraically closed field have no common zero iff some polynomial combination $\sum_i g_i f_i$ equals $1$.

entry_2.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, a system of affine polynomial equations has an empty solution set exactly when the ideal it generates already contains $1$.

entry_1.statement: A polynomial vanishes on every common zero of a system of polynomials iff some power of it lies in the ideal generated by the system.

entry_2.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, every regular function forced to vanish on the common solution locus of an equation-generated constraint already has a positive exponent lying in that constraint.

pairs.topic: Regular function / Element of coordinate ring

entry_1.statement: A regular function on $V$ is a polynomial function $V \to k$, i.e., the restriction to $V$ of a polynomial in the ambient coordinates.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, such a function is a residue class in the coordinate algebra obtained after quotienting ambient polynomials by those vanishing identically on $V$.

entry_1.statement: Polynomial maps $V \to W$ between affine varieties.

entry_2.statement: On coordinate algebras, a morphism of affine varieties is seen contravariantly as pullback of regular functions from the target algebra to the source algebra.

entry_1.statement: The Cartesian product $V \times W$ is again an affine variety.

entry_2.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, forming the product of affine varieties on the geometric side corresponds contravariantly to taking the tensor product of their coordinate algebras over the ground field.

entry_1.statement: For closed subvarieties of $\mathbb{A}^n$, $W_1 \subseteq W_2$ iff every regular function vanishing on $W_2$ also vanishes on $W_1$.

entry_2.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, the inclusion order on affine closed sets is reversed by the operation sending a closed set to all polynomials that vanish on it.

entry_1.statement: The set $D(f) = \{p \in V : f(p) \neq 0\}$ is itself an affine variety.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, restricting to the region where a regular function is nonzero is accomplished by adjoining an inverse for that function in the coordinate algebra.

entry_1.statement: The Zariski tangent space to $V$ at a point $p$ is the $k$-vector space of $k$-linear derivations $k[V] \to k$ centered at $p$.

entry_2.statement: At a closed point $p$, first-order infinitesimal directions are the $k$-linear dual of the cotangent space obtained from the maximal ideal modulo its square.

entry_1.statement: A point $p$ of $V$ is smooth iff the dimension of the tangent space at $p$ equals the dimension of $V$ at $p$.

entry_2.statement: Smoothness at $p$ is detected algebraically by the local coordinate ring: its embedding dimension, measured by the minimal number of generators of the maximal ideal, must equal its Krull dimension.

entry_1.statement: An affine variety is connected iff it is not the disjoint union of two nonempty closed subvarieties.

entry_2.statement: The coordinate algebra cannot split nontrivially by an idempotent; its only elements satisfying $e^2=e$ are the two trivial ones.

entry_1.statement: The affine scheme associated to an irreducible affine variety has a unique generic point whose closure is the whole space.

entry_2.statement: For the coordinate domain of an irreducible affine variety, the prime ideal $(0)$ is the generic point of the associated affine scheme.

pairs.topic: Disjoint union / Direct product of rings

entry_1.statement: The disjoint union of two affine algebraic sets is again affine.

entry_2.statement: On the algebra side, separating an affine object into two open-and-closed pieces corresponds to replacing its coordinate algebra by a finite direct product of the two coordinate algebras.

entry_1.statement: The function field of an irreducible affine variety $V$ consists of ratios of regular functions, identified when they agree on a dense open set.

entry_2.statement: For a coordinate algebra that is a domain, rational functions live in the total fraction field obtained after allowing every nonzero regular function to serve as a denominator.

pairs.topic: Local ring at a point / Localization at a maximal ideal

entry_1.statement: The local ring of $V$ at $p$ consists of rational functions defined on some open neighborhood of $p$.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, focusing near $p$ means localizing the coordinate algebra away from the maximal ideal corresponding to $p$, so precisely the functions nonvanishing at $p$ become invertible.

entry_1.statement: The space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ with coordinates $x_1, \ldots, x_n$.

entry_2.statement: Its coordinate algebra is the polynomial algebra characterized by freely adjoining $n$ independent coordinate functions to the field $k$.

entry_1.statement: A hypersurface in $\mathbb{A}^n$ is the vanishing locus of a single nonconstant polynomial.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, one equation in affine space is recorded by the ideal generated by a single nonzero nonunit polynomial, with the underlying closed set depending only on its radical.

entry_1.statement: Every descending chain of closed subvarieties of an affine variety stabilizes.

entry_2.statement: Hilbert's basis theorem makes every finitely generated $k$-algebra Noetherian, so its ideals cannot form an infinite strictly increasing chain.

pairs.topic: Birational equivalence / Isomorphism of fraction fields

entry_1.statement: Two irreducible affine varieties contain isomorphic Zariski-dense open subsets.

entry_2.statement: For irreducible affine varieties, agreeing after removing lower-dimensional closed pieces is detected by an isomorphism between the fraction fields of their coordinate domains.

entry_1.statement: The codimension of an irreducible closed subvariety $W$ in an irreducible variety $V$ is $\dim V - \dim W$.

entry_2.statement: For the prime ideal defining an irreducible closed subset of an affine domain, codimension is measured algebraically by the largest length of a strictly increasing chain of prime ideals ending at that prime.

entry_1.statement: A morphism of affine varieties whose coordinate functions satisfy finite algebraic dependence over the functions pulled back from the target.

entry_2.statement: Contravariantly, the pullback on coordinate rings turns the source algebra into a module generated by finitely many elements over the target algebra.

entry_1.statement: For an irreducible affine variety $V$, there exists a unique normal variety equipped with a finite birational morphism to $V$.

entry_2.statement: For a Noetherian coordinate domain, normalization is obtained by adjoining all elements of its fraction field that satisfy monic equations with coefficients in the original ring.

pairs.topic: Dimension via chains of subvarieties / Krull dimension

entry_1.statement: The dimension of an irreducible affine variety $V$ is the supremum, over chains $\emptyset \neq V_0 \subsetneq V_1 \subsetneq \cdots \subsetneq V_n = V$ of irreducible closed subvarieties, of $n$.

entry_2.statement: The Krull invariant of a ring is the largest length obtainable from a finite strictly increasing sequence of prime ideals.

entry_1.statement: An injective morphism $W \hookrightarrow V$ of affine varieties identifying $W$ with a closed subvariety.

entry_2.statement: On coordinate algebras, realizing one affine variety as a closed subvariety of another is exactly the contravariant operation of quotienting the larger coordinate algebra.

pairs.topic: Vanishing of a function at a point / Membership in a maximal ideal

entry_1.statement: A regular function $f \in k[V]$ vanishes at a point $p$.

entry_2.statement: Under evaluation at $p$, this regular function maps to zero in the residue field, equivalently it belongs to the kernel maximal ideal attached to $p$.

entry_1.statement: Every loop in $S^1$ is determined up to homotopy by an integer counting net wrap-around, so $\pi_1(S^1) \cong \mathbb{Z}$.

entry_2.statement: For the covering $\mathbb{R}\to S^1$ given by quotienting by unit translations, the covering symmetries are exactly translations by integers.

entry_1.statement: For $n \geq 2$, every loop in $S^n$ contracts to a point.

entry_2.statement: For $n \geq 2$, the universal covering of $S^n$ is already $S^n$ itself, so no nontrivial connected cover sits above it.

entry_1.statement: For a nice pointed space $(X, x_0)$, isomorphism classes of pointed connected coverings of $X$ are in bijection with subgroups of $\pi_1(X, x_0)$.

entry_2.statement: For a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space, connected covers are recovered from subgroups of the group of covering symmetries of the universal cover, with larger subgroups giving smaller intermediate quotients.

entry_1.statement: A connected covering $p : Y \to X$ is regular iff the image subgroup $p_*\pi_1(Y) \subseteq \pi_1(X)$ is normal.

entry_2.statement: In the subgroup dictionary for connected covers, the covers whose automorphism group moves any chosen point of a fiber to any other are exactly those represented by conjugation-invariant subgroups.

entry_1.statement: A continuous map $f : (X, x) \to (Y, y)$ induces a group homomorphism $f_* : \pi_1(X, x) \to \pi_1(Y, y)$ respecting composition.

entry_2.statement: Passing from a pointed space to its loop classes is functorial: homotopic pointed maps give the same group map, and composing pointed maps corresponds to composing the induced algebra homomorphisms.

entry_1.statement: $\pi_1(X \times Y, (x, y)) \cong \pi_1(X, x) \times \pi_1(Y, y)$.

entry_2.statement: For suitably nice connected spaces, taking universal covers commutes with finite products, and the covering symmetries of the resulting product split componentwise.

entry_1.statement: For $X = U \cup V$ with $U, V$ open and $U, V, U \cap V$ path-connected, $\pi_1(X) \cong \pi_1(U) *_{\pi_1(U \cap V)} \pi_1(V)$.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, gluing two path-connected pieces along a path-connected overlap is mirrored by the categorical pushout of the two induced group maps from the overlap group.

entry_1.statement: The fundamental group of a wedge of $n$ circles is the free group on $n$ generators.

entry_2.statement: The deck transformations of the universal cover of an $n$-petaled rose act on the covering tree by freely reduced words in $n$ letters, with no relations beyond cancellation.

entry_1.statement: The fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 1$ has $2g$ generators (one per ``$a_i$'' and ``$b_i$'' loop) satisfying a single relation from the boundary of a $4g$-gon.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, the corresponding fundamental group is obtained from the free group on $2g$ named generators by imposing one relator: the product of the paired commutators is trivial.

entry_1.statement: For every group $G$, there exists a connected CW complex $K(G, 1)$ with $\pi_1 = G$ and all higher homotopy groups trivial, unique up to homotopy equivalence.

entry_2.statement: Every group admits a free properly discontinuous action on a contractible CW complex whose quotient has that group as its only nontrivial homotopy group.

entry_1.statement: For a path-connected space $X$, the first homology group is obtained from $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ by forcing all loop classes to commute.

entry_2.statement: The universal abelian quotient of a group is formed by killing exactly the subgroup generated by all commutators.

entry_1.statement: The fundamental group of any topological group is abelian.

entry_2.statement: Whenever a group carries a second group law that is compatible with the first in the Eckmann-Hilton sense, the two laws coincide and become commutative.

entry_1.statement: Every connected covering of $S^1$ is either the $n$-fold cyclic cover $z \mapsto z^n$ for some $n \geq 1$, or the universal cover $\mathbb{R} \to S^1$.

entry_2.statement: The subgroup lattice of the infinite cyclic group consists of the finite-index multiples $n\mathbb{Z}$ together with the zero subgroup.

entry_1.statement: For a regular covering $p : Y \to X$ with $Y$ path-connected, the deck transformation group acts freely and transitively on each fiber $p^{-1}(x)$.

entry_2.statement: A group, viewed as a set with its left-regular action, is a torsor for itself: each ordered pair of points determines a unique acting element.

entry_1.statement: Each loop in $X$ based at $x_0$ induces a permutation of the fiber over $x_0$ by lifting the loop and recording endpoints.

entry_2.statement: For a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space, covering spaces can be reconstructed from sets equipped with the monodromy action of the fundamental group.

entry_1.statement: $\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ for $n \geq 2$, generated by a non-contractible loop.

entry_2.statement: For $n\geq2$, the double cover $S^n\to\mathbb{RP}^n$ has covering symmetry group of order two, generated by the antipodal map.

entry_1.statement: $\pi_1$ of the $n$-torus $T^n = (S^1)^n$ is $\mathbb{Z}^n$.

entry_2.statement: The universal cover of the $n$-torus is Euclidean space, and its covering symmetries are precisely lattice translations by integer vectors.

pairs.topic: Degree of self-maps of the circle

entry_1.statement: Pointed homotopy classes of maps $S^1 \to S^1$ are classified by an integer called the degree.

entry_2.statement: An endomorphism of the infinite cyclic group is completely determined by the image of a generator, hence by a single integer.

entry_1.statement: For pointed connected CW complexes with non-degenerate basepoints, $\pi_1(X \vee Y) \cong \pi_1(X) * \pi_1(Y)$.

entry_2.statement: In the category of groups, the object receiving homomorphisms from two given groups without imposing extra relations between their images is their free product.

entry_1.statement: A continuous $f : (Z, z) \to (X, x)$ from a path-connected, locally path-connected $Z$ lifts through a covering $p : (Y, y) \to (X, x)$ iff $f_*\pi_1(Z) \subseteq p_*\pi_1(Y)$.

entry_2.statement: For an inclusion of groups $H\leq\Gamma$, a map into $\Gamma$ comes from a map into $H$ exactly when its image never leaves $H$.

entry_1.statement: For a self-homeomorphism $f : X \to X$, the mapping torus has fundamental group an HNN extension of $\pi_1(X)$ with stable letter conjugating by $f_*$.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, suspending an automorphism of a group amounts to adjoining one new generator whose conjugation action implements that automorphism.

entry_1.statement: For $n \geq 2$, $\pi_n(X, x_0)$ is abelian.

entry_2.statement: Eckmann-Hilton says that two unital compositions on the same objects, when they interchange compatibly, collapse to one commutative operation.

entry_1.statement: A path-connected space is simply connected iff every loop is null-homotopic.

entry_2.statement: Under the covering-subgroup correspondence, the simply connected cover is represented by the identity subgroup of the fundamental group.

entry_1.statement: The set of free homotopy classes of self-homotopy-equivalences of a $K(G, 1)$ space is in bijection with $\mathrm{Out}(G)$.

entry_2.statement: For a group $G$, changing an automorphism by conjugation inside $G$ does not change the corresponding unpointed self-equivalence of a $K(G,1)$; the quotient by these inner changes is the invariant.

entry_1.statement: For a connected covering $p : Y \to X$, the cardinality of any fiber equals $[\pi_1(X) : p_*\pi_1(Y)]$.

entry_2.statement: A transitive group action identifies the underlying set with the coset space of any point stabilizer, so its size is the corresponding subgroup index.

entry_1.statement: Two based loops in $X$ are freely homotopic iff they represent conjugate elements of $\pi_1(X, x_0)$.

entry_2.statement: When a basepoint on a loop is allowed to slide around the loop, the associated group element is remembered only up to the orbit relation given by conjugation.

entry_1.statement: For every presentation $\langle S \mid R \rangle$ of a group $G$, there is a 2-dimensional CW complex with one 0-cell, one 1-cell per generator, and one 2-cell per relator, having fundamental group $G$.

entry_2.statement: Algebraically, attaching relators to a free group means quotienting the free group on the chosen generators by the normal subgroup generated by the listed words.

entry_1.statement: There is a fiber bundle $S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3 \twoheadrightarrow S^2$ with structure group $S^1$.

entry_2.statement: Viewing $S^3$ as unit quaternions, quotienting by the free circle action coming from unit complex scalars produces the base $S^2$.

entry_1.statement: Unpointed isomorphism classes of connected coverings of $X$ correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of subgroups of $\pi_1(X)$.

entry_2.statement: Each transitive $G$-action is classified, up to $G$-equivariant equivalence, by the stabilizer subgroup of any chosen point, and changing the chosen point conjugates that subgroup.

entry_1.statement: Two connected CW complexes that are both $K(G, 1)$'s for the same group $G$ are homotopy equivalent.

entry_2.statement: An aspherical connected CW complex is determined up to homotopy by its fundamental group: any isomorphism of the groups is realized by a homotopy equivalence.

entry_1.statement: $G$ is bipartite iff it contains no cycle of odd length.

entry_2.statement: For a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, the eigenvalue multiset is invariant under multiplication by $-1$.

entry_1.statement: The number of walks of length $k$ from vertex $i$ to vertex $j$ in $G$.

entry_2.statement: After multiplying the adjacency matrix by itself $k$ times, the entry in row $i$ and column $j$ records exactly this combinatorial count.

entry_1.statement: The total number of closed walks of length $k$ in $G$ summed over all starting vertices.

entry_2.statement: Taking the trace of the $k$th adjacency-matrix power aggregates the diagonal walk counts, equivalently the $k$th power sum of the adjacency eigenvalues.

entry_1.statement: The number of triangles in $G$.

entry_2.statement: For a simple undirected graph, closed adjacency walks of length three enumerate each triangular subgraph six times.

entry_1.statement: The number of edges of $G$.

entry_2.statement: For a simple undirected graph, the second spectral moment of the adjacency matrix counts oriented traversals of edges, so half of it gives the edge count.

entry_1.statement: Every vertex of $G$ has the same degree $d$.

entry_2.statement: The constant vector is an adjacency eigenvector with eigenvalue $d$, meaning all row sums of the adjacency matrix are equal to $d$.

entry_1.statement: The number of connected components of $G$.

entry_2.statement: The Laplacian has a nullspace consisting of functions constant on each component, so the zero-eigenspace dimension records this number.

entry_1.statement: $G$ is connected.

entry_2.statement: The Laplacian has a one-dimensional kernel, equivalently its only zero-energy vectors are globally constant.

entry_1.statement: There is a vertex bijection $G \to G'$ preserving adjacency.

entry_2.statement: Relabeling vertices corresponds exactly to conjugating the adjacency matrix by a permutation matrix.

entry_1.statement: The number of spanning trees of $G$.

entry_2.statement: Kirchhoff's theorem computes this count by deleting one row and column from the Laplacian and taking the resulting determinant; equivalently it is $n^{-1}$ times the product of the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues.

entry_1.statement: For $S \subseteq V$, the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$.

entry_2.statement: Evaluating the Laplacian quadratic form on the $0$-$1$ vector of $S$ counts exactly the edges crossing from $S$ to its complement.

entry_1.statement: The number of neighbors of vertex $i$.

entry_2.statement: In the adjacency matrix, summing the entries across row $i$ gives the valence of the corresponding vertex.

entry_1.statement: The complement $\overline G$ has the same vertices as $G$, with $uv$ an edge iff it is not an edge of $G$ (and $u \neq v$).

entry_2.statement: At the matrix level, passing to the complement replaces every off-diagonal adjacency entry by its opposite and leaves the diagonal at zero.

entry_1.statement: The Cartesian product $G \,\square\, H$ has vertex set $V(G) \times V(H)$, with $(u,v)$ adjacent to $(u',v')$ iff either $u = u'$ and $vv' \in E(H)$, or $v = v'$ and $uu' \in E(G)$.

entry_2.statement: For the Cartesian product, the adjacency operator changes one coordinate at a time, so it is the Kronecker sum of the two factor adjacency operators and has pairwise summed eigenvalues.

entry_1.statement: The tensor product $G \times H$ has vertex set $V(G) \times V(H)$, with $(u,v)$ adjacent to $(u',v')$ iff $uu' \in E(G)$ and $vv' \in E(H)$.

entry_2.statement: For the tensor product, adjacency requires simultaneous motion in both factors, which makes the adjacency operator the Kronecker product and multiplies the two spectra pairwise.

entry_1.statement: $G \sqcup H$ has the vertices and edges of $G$ and $H$ kept separate.

entry_2.statement: Keeping two graphs separate makes the adjacency operator decompose as a direct sum, so its eigenvalue multiset is obtained by pooling those of the two pieces.

entry_1.statement: The $n$-vertex cycle $C_n$.

entry_2.statement: The adjacency operator of $C_n$ is diagonalized by the discrete Fourier modes on the cyclic group, with eigenvalues $2\cos(2\pi k/n)$.

entry_1.statement: The $n$-vertex path $P_n$.

entry_2.statement: The tridiagonal adjacency matrix of $P_n$ has the sine-basis spectrum $2\cos(k\pi/(n+1))$ for $1\leq k\leq n$.

entry_1.statement: The complete graph on $n$ vertices.

entry_2.statement: Its adjacency operator acts by $n-1$ on the constant line and by $-1$ on the hyperplane of vectors whose coordinates sum to zero.

entry_1.statement: $G$ is $k$-regular; every pair of adjacent vertices has exactly $\lambda$ common neighbors, and every pair of non-adjacent distinct vertices has exactly $\mu$ common neighbors.

entry_2.statement: For the adjacency matrix, the diagonal of $A^2$ records $k$, entries on adjacent pairs record $\lambda$, and entries on nonadjacent off-diagonal pairs record $\mu$; equivalently these counts combine into the standard quadratic identity for $A$.

entry_1.statement: A vertex bijection $\sigma : V \to V$ with $uv \in E \iff \sigma(u)\sigma(v) \in E$.

entry_2.statement: In matrix language, such a symmetry is exactly a coordinate permutation whose operator commutes with the adjacency operator.

entry_1.statement: The diameter of a connected $G$ is the maximum of shortest-path distances.

entry_2.statement: If the adjacency operator of a connected graph has only $s$ different spectral values, then no two vertices can be farther apart than $s-1$.

entry_1.statement: At each step, a token at vertex $v$ moves to a uniformly random neighbor of $v$.

entry_2.statement: The one-step Markov operator is obtained by normalizing each adjacency row by the degree of its source vertex.

entry_1.statement: $G$ is connected.

entry_2.statement: For a finite graph, connectedness is the same as irreducibility of its nonnegative adjacency matrix; Perron-Frobenius then gives a unique positive eigenline at the spectral radius.

entry_1.statement: A connected graph $G$ is bipartite.

entry_2.statement: For a connected graph, bipartiteness is detected spectrally by the two extremal adjacency eigenvalues being antipodal; each endpoint eigenvalue occurs with multiplicity one.

entry_1.statement: Orient each edge of $G$ arbitrarily; record the resulting vertex-edge incidence pattern in a matrix $B$ with rows indexed by vertices, columns by oriented edges, entries in $\{-1, 0, +1\}$.

entry_2.statement: Multiplying the signed incidence matrix by its transpose recovers the graph Laplacian, and the result does not depend on which directions were assigned to the edges.

entry_1.statement: The automorphism group of $G$ acts transitively on vertices.

entry_2.statement: Equivalently, among the coordinate permutations that commute with the adjacency operator, there is a subgroup moving any standard basis vector to any other.

entry_1.statement: The star graph $K_{1,n}$ with one center connected to $n$ leaves.

entry_2.statement: Its adjacency operator has rank two on the span of the center and the uniform leaf vector, giving eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt n$, and vanishes on the remaining leaf-difference subspace.

pairs.topic: Regular Laplacian / Affine shift of adjacency spectrum

entry_1.statement: $G$ is $d$-regular.

entry_2.statement: When all degrees equal $d$, the Laplacian is just the adjacency operator shifted and negated by $dI$, so the eigenvectors are unchanged and eigenvalues transform by $\lambda\mapsto d-\lambda$.

pairs.topic: Bipartite double cover / Off-diagonal block matrix

entry_1.statement: The bipartite double cover of $G$ has vertex set $V \times \{0, 1\}$, with $(u, 0)$ and $(v, 1)$ adjacent iff $uv \in E(G)$.

entry_2.statement: With the two vertex copies ordered as blocks, the adjacency operator is off-diagonal with $A$ in both off-diagonal positions; every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ therefore contributes the pair $\lambda$ and $-\lambda$.

entry_1.statement: The number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts equals the number of partitions of $n$ into odd parts.

entry_2.statement: The ordinary generating function obtained by allowing each part at most once coincides with the one obtained by allowing unrestricted odd part sizes.

entry_1.statement: The number of $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set is $\binom{n}{k}$.

entry_2.statement: Expanding the $n$-fold product of identical two-term choices, the coefficient of degree $k$ records choosing the second term in exactly $k$ factors.

entry_1.statement: The number of ordered tuples $(a_1, \ldots, a_k)$ of positive integers with $a_1 + \cdots + a_k = n$, summed over $k \geq 1$, equals $2^{n-1}$.

entry_2.statement: A part of size at least one contributes $x+x^2+\cdots$, and allowing a nonempty sequence of such parts sums to the rational series $x/(1-2x)$.

entry_1.statement: The number of properly nested sequences of $n$ pairs of parentheses.

entry_2.statement: The ordinary generating series for these objects is the unique power series with constant term $1$ satisfying the quadratic decomposition equation $C=1+xC^2$.

entry_1.statement: The number of ways to tile a $1 \times n$ strip with $1 \times 1$ squares and $1 \times 2$ dominoes.

entry_2.statement: The ordinary generating series for these tilings is the reciprocal of $1-x-x^2$, reflecting the choice of a final tile of length one or two.

entry_1.statement: The number of unordered ways to write $n$ as a sum of positive integers.

entry_2.statement: The unrestricted partition numbers are encoded by the infinite Euler product whose $k$th factor permits any multiplicity of parts of size $k$.

pairs.topic: Inclusion-exclusion / Sign-alternating sum of generating functions

entry_1.statement: For events $A_1, \ldots, A_n$, $|A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n| = \sum_i |A_i| - \sum_{i<j} |A_i \cap A_j| + \cdots$.

entry_2.statement: At the level of indicators, membership in at least one set is expressed by expanding one minus the product of the complementary indicators and then summing over the finite universe.

pairs.topic: Stirling numbers of the second kind / Exponential generating function

entry_1.statement: $S(n, k)$ counts the number of partitions of an $n$-element set into $k$ nonempty unordered blocks.

entry_2.statement: In exponential generating functions, choosing exactly $k$ label-carrying groups, each of size at least one and with no order among the groups, contributes $(e^x-1)^k/k!$.

entry_1.statement: $B_n$ is the total number of partitions of an $n$-element set.

entry_2.statement: Allowing an arbitrary set of nonempty labeled blocks gives the exponential generating function obtained by exponentiating $e^x-1$.

entry_1.statement: The fraction of permutations of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ with no fixed point approaches $1/e$ as $n \to \infty$.

entry_2.statement: The derangement exponential generating function is $e^{-x}/(1-x)$; its dominant simple pole at $x=1$ has residue scaled by $e^{-1}$, giving $D_n/n! \to e^{-1}$.

pairs.topic: Vandermonde's identity / Coefficient of a product

entry_1.statement: $\binom{m + n}{k} = \displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{k} \binom{m}{j}\binom{n}{k - j}$.

entry_2.statement: Multiplying two binomial generating polynomials and extracting the degree-$k$ term gives the same result as first combining the exponents.

entry_1.statement: $\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n-1}{k-1} + \binom{n-1}{k}$.

entry_2.statement: Separating the last binary choice in the binomial generating polynomial yields the two adjacent coefficients from the previous degree.

entry_1.statement: The number of orderings of an $n$-element set is $n!$.

entry_2.statement: As an exponential generating function, permutations are encoded by $1/(1-x)$, so the coefficient multiplying $x^n/n!$ is $n!$.

entry_1.statement: The number $D_n$ of permutations of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ with no fixed point.

entry_2.statement: The exponential generating function for fixed-point-free permutations is obtained by multiplying the permutation EGF by the exclusion factor $e^{-x}$.

entry_1.statement: If $a_n$ counts objects of weight $n$ in family $\mathcal{A}$ and $b_n$ does so for $\mathcal{B}$, then $\sum_{k = 0}^n a_k b_{n-k}$ counts ordered pairs in $\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}$ of total weight $n$.

entry_2.statement: Ordinary generating functions turn pairing two weighted classes into multiplication, with total weight distributed between the two factors in all possible ways.

entry_1.statement: The number of partitions of $n$ grows like $\dfrac{1}{4n\sqrt{3}} \exp\!\left(\pi\sqrt{\tfrac{2n}{3}}\right)$ as $n \to \infty$.

entry_2.statement: The leading Hardy-Ramanujan term comes from analyzing Euler's partition product near its dominant singularity at $x=1$ using the circle method.

entry_1.statement: The number of paths from $(0, 0)$ to $(m, n)$ using right-steps and up-steps is $\binom{m + n}{m}$.

entry_2.statement: The bivariate ordinary generating function $1/(1-x-y)$ expands by recording one variable for each horizontal step and the other for each vertical step.

pairs.topic: Multinomial coefficients / Power of a sum

entry_1.statement: The number of ways to color $n$ objects with $k$ colors, using color $i$ exactly $n_i$ times where $\sum n_i = n$, is $\dfrac{n!}{n_1!\, n_2! \cdots n_k!}$.

entry_2.statement: Expanding the $n$th power of the sum of $k$ color variables, the monomial with exponents $n_1,\ldots,n_k$ appears with the multinomial coefficient.

pairs.topic: Sum of geometric / Counting binary strings

entry_1.statement: The number of binary strings of length $\leq n$ is $2^{n+1} - 1$.

entry_2.statement: Summing the counts by length gives a finite geometric progression with ratio two and last exponent $n$.

entry_1.statement: The number of rooted labeled trees on $n$ vertices is $n^{n-1}$.

entry_2.statement: The tree function solving $T=x\exp(T)$ has exponential-generating coefficients extracted by Lagrange inversion, yielding $n^{n-1}$ for size $n$.

entry_1.statement: $B_{n+1} = \displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} B_k$.

entry_2.statement: Differentiating the Bell-number exponential generating function multiplies it by $e^x$, and comparing coefficients gives the binomial recurrence.

entry_1.statement: The number of partitions of $n$ equal to their conjugate equals the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct odd parts.

entry_2.statement: The ordinary generating product that allows each odd part size either zero or one time also enumerates Ferrers diagrams symmetric about the main diagonal.

entry_1.statement: The total number of subsets of an $n$-element set is $2^n$.

entry_2.statement: The binomial generating polynomial for choosing elements from an $n$-set totals all subset sizes when the marking variable is set to one.

entry_1.statement: The number of $n$-cycles in $S_n$ is $(n-1)!$.

entry_2.statement: The labeled-cycle exponential generating function is the logarithm of the reciprocal of $1-x$, whose degree-$n$ term has weight $1/n$.

entry_1.statement: If a labeled combinatorial class is built by taking sets of ``connected'' pieces of weight $\geq 1$, the EGF of the class equals the exponential of the EGF of the connected pieces.

entry_2.statement: At the level of EGFs, allowing an arbitrary finite collection of connected label-carrying components turns the component series $C(x)$ into the total series $\exp(C(x))$.

pairs.topic: Number of permutations with $k$ cycles / Signless Stirling

entry_1.statement: The number of permutations of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ with exactly $k$ cycles, denoted $c(n, k)$ or $\left[\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k}\right]$.

entry_2.statement: Marking each cycle by a variable $y$ changes the permutation EGF to $(1-x)^{-y}$, whose bivariate coefficients recover the signless Stirling numbers.

entry_1.statement: The number of partitions of $n$ into an even number of distinct parts minus the number into an odd number of distinct parts equals $(-1)^k$ if $n = k(3k \pm 1)/2$ and $0$ otherwise.

entry_2.statement: Euler's product assigning a negative sign to each used part has nonzero coefficients only at generalized pentagonal exponents, where the sign is determined by the corresponding integer parameter.

pairs.topic: Cauchy's coefficient formula / Counting by integration

entry_1.statement: The number of objects of weight $n$ in a class with generating function $A(x)$.

entry_2.statement: Analytically, the weight-$n$ coefficient of a generating function is isolated by integrating the function against $z^{-n-1}$ around the origin.

entry_1.statement: For $n \geq 1$, the number of subsets of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ with an even number of elements equals $2^{n-1}$.

entry_2.statement: A parity filter formed by averaging the subset enumerator at $x=1$ and $x=-1$ keeps exactly the even-cardinality terms.

pairs.topic: Necklaces / Mobius and roots of unity

entry_1.statement: The number of $k$-bead necklaces with $q$ colors, where rotations are identified.

entry_2.statement: Burnside averaging over the rotation group counts colorings fixed by each rotation; grouping rotations by cycle structure gives $k^{-1}\sum_{d\mid k}\varphi(d)q^{k/d}$.

entry_1.statement: For a locally compact abelian group $G$, the set of continuous homomorphisms $G \to \mathbb{T}$ forms a topological group $\hat G$, and the canonical map $G \to \hat{\hat G}$ is an isomorphism.

entry_2.statement: For signals on a time group satisfying the usual Pontryagin-duality hypotheses, the frequency variables themselves form a dual character group, and applying the same construction again recovers the original domain.

entry_1.statement: The Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{Z}$ is $\mathbb{T}$, with the character indexed by $\theta \in \mathbb{T}$ sending $n \mapsto e^{2\pi i n \theta}$.

entry_2.statement: For integer-indexed signals, the frequency parameter is circular: each point of the unit circle gives the elementary mode whose $n$th sample is its $n$th power.

entry_1.statement: The Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{T}$ is $\mathbb{Z}$, with characters $\theta \mapsto e^{2\pi i n \theta}$ indexed by $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

entry_2.statement: Fourier modes on a circle are indexed by integers, so the frequency side of a compact one-dimensional torus is a discrete lattice.

entry_1.statement: $\widehat{\mathbb{R}} \cong \mathbb{R}$, via $\xi \mapsto (x \mapsto e^{2\pi i \xi x})$.

entry_2.statement: The real line is self-dual under Fourier analysis: every real frequency labels the plane-wave character $x\mapsto e^{2\pi i\xi x}$.

entry_1.statement: $\widehat{\mathbb{Z}/n} \cong \mathbb{Z}/n$, with characters $k \mapsto e^{2\pi i j k / n}$ for $j \in \mathbb{Z}/n$.

entry_2.statement: For length-$n$ cyclic data, the Fourier basis consists of the $n$ roots-of-unity waves, one for each residue class modulo $n$.

entry_1.statement: For a finite group $G$, the irreducible characters form an orthonormal basis of the space of class functions under the inner product $\langle \chi, \psi \rangle = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_g \chi(g) \overline{\psi(g)}$.

entry_2.statement: In the finite-group Fourier transform, irreducible character modes are mutually orthogonal, and class functions expand uniquely in that orthonormal character basis.

entry_1.statement: For a locally compact abelian group $G$ with appropriate normalizations of Haar measure, the Fourier transform is an isometry $L^2(G) \to L^2(\hat G)$.

entry_2.statement: With invariant measures normalized compatibly, the passage from a signal to its frequency-side representative preserves the $L^2$ norm, so signal energy is unchanged.

entry_1.statement: For functions $f, g \in L^1(G)$ on a locally compact abelian group, $\widehat{f * g} = \hat f \cdot \hat g$.

entry_2.statement: The Fourier transform diagonalizes translation-invariant averaging: convolution on the group side becomes pointwise multiplication on the character side.

entry_1.statement: For sufficiently nice $f$ on a locally compact abelian group $G$, $f(x) = \int_{\hat G} \hat f(\chi)\, \chi(x)\, d\chi$.

entry_2.statement: For functions in an appropriate inversion class, the original signal is recovered by integrating its frequency amplitudes against the corresponding characters.

entry_1.statement: For a compact group $G$, matrix coefficients of irreducible unitary representations form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(G)$.

entry_2.statement: On a compact topological group, the functions obtained as entries of finite-dimensional irreducible norm-preserving actions span a dense subspace of $L^2$, and after normalization they give the standard Hilbert-space decomposition.

entry_1.statement: On a locally compact abelian group $G$, the translation operators $T_a f(x) = f(x - a)$ are jointly diagonalized by the characters $\chi : G \to \mathbb{T}$, with eigenvalue $\chi(a)$.

entry_2.statement: After Fourier transform, every shift operator acts diagonally: each frequency coordinate is merely rescaled by a unit complex phase.

entry_1.statement: For a closed subgroup $H \leq G$ with quotient $G/H$, summing a function over $H$ is dual to summing its Fourier transform over the annihilator $H^\perp \subseteq \hat G$.

entry_2.statement: Periodizing a function along a lattice on the time side becomes summation over the reciprocal lattice after passing to frequency variables.

entry_1.statement: On $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, the position and momentum operators satisfy $[\hat x, \hat p] = i\hbar$, and no nonzero function is jointly localized at a point in both spectra.

entry_2.statement: Time concentration and frequency concentration obey an uncertainty bound: a nonzero waveform cannot be arbitrarily sharp in both conjugate variables.

entry_1.statement: A continuous function $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ on a locally compact abelian group is positive definite iff it is the Fourier transform of a finite nonneg. measure on $\hat G$.

entry_2.statement: Autocorrelation kernels are exactly those represented by unsigned spectral distributions, so the corresponding frequency content has no signed part.

entry_1.statement: Every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U_t$ on a Hilbert space has the form $U_t = e^{itA}$ for a unique self-adjoint operator $A$.

entry_2.statement: A continuous energy-preserving flow on the state space is obtained by exponentiating its spectral generator, so the associated coordinates rotate with linear phases.

entry_1.statement: For locally compact abelian groups $G$ and $H$, $\widehat{G \times H} \cong \hat G \times \hat H$.

entry_2.statement: For independent group coordinates, a frequency is a tuple of one frequency from each factor, so multi-variable Fourier analysis separates by coordinate.

entry_1.statement: For a locally compact abelian group $G$, $G$ is compact iff $\hat G$ is discrete; $G$ is discrete iff $\hat G$ is compact.

entry_2.statement: Compactness of the time domain forces frequency labels to be isolated, while a discrete time domain produces a compact frequency space.

entry_1.statement: Any unitary representation of a compact group decomposes uniquely as an orthogonal direct sum of isotypic components indexed by irreducible representations.

entry_2.statement: A Hilbert space carrying compact symmetries splits orthogonally into frequency blocks indexed by irreducible symmetry types.

entry_1.statement: For $f \in L^1(G)$ on a locally compact abelian group, $\hat f$ is continuous on $\hat G$ and vanishes at infinity.

entry_2.statement: The transform of an integrable signal is a continuous frequency function whose values become arbitrarily small far from the origin.

entry_1.statement: On a compact group $G$, conjugation-invariant functions are spanned by irreducible characters.

entry_2.statement: On a compact group, functions constant on conjugacy classes are precisely the central part of the Fourier expansion, spanned by character traces rather than individual matrix entries.

entry_1.statement: For a function on $\mathbb{R}$ whose Fourier support lies in a compact interval $[-W, W]$, the values on the discrete subgroup $\tfrac{1}{2W}\mathbb{Z}$ determine the function uniquely.

entry_2.statement: If no frequencies occur outside $[-W,W]$, sampling at spacing $1/(2W)$ contains enough information to reconstruct the entire waveform.

pairs.topic: Tensor product of representations / Product of signals

entry_1.statement: The tensor product of two unitary representations of an abelian group $G$ decomposes into characters via $\chi \otimes \psi \mapsto \chi \cdot \psi$.

entry_2.statement: Pointwise multiplication before analysis corresponds, after transforming, to combining frequency amplitudes by convolution.

entry_1.statement: For a closed subgroup $H \leq G$ of a locally compact abelian group, $\widehat{G/H} \cong H^\perp \subseteq \hat G$.

entry_2.statement: Functions that do not change along cosets of $H$ have spectral support only on characters that are trivial when restricted to $H$.

entry_1.statement: Closed subgroups of $G$ correspond bijectively to closed quotient groups of $\hat G$ via the annihilator construction.

entry_2.statement: Passing from a time-domain group to a subgroup or factor group reverses on the frequency side through the operation of taking characters that vanish there.

pairs.topic: Group algebra / Function algebra under convolution

entry_1.statement: The group algebra $L^1(G)$ under convolution is a commutative Banach algebra when $G$ is abelian.

entry_2.statement: For commutative time domains, the frequency-side map turns integrable waveforms with their usual integral product into ordinary multiplication of frequency functions.

entry_1.statement: The continuous irreducible unitary representations of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are one-dimensional, labeled by $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^n$, given by $x \mapsto e^{2\pi i \langle \xi, x \rangle}$.

entry_2.statement: In Euclidean signal analysis, the indecomposable oscillatory modes are plane waves, one for each frequency vector in the dual Euclidean space.

entry_1.statement: For a continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of a compact group $G$ on a Hilbert space $V$, the projection to the trivial isotypic component is $\int_G \pi(g)\, dg$.

entry_2.statement: Averaging over the compact symmetry removes every nontrivial harmonic component and leaves only the invariant, zero-frequency part.

entry_1.statement: For an abelian group, the natural action of $G$ on $L^2(\hat G)$ by modulation is unitarily equivalent, via Fourier transform, to the regular representation of $G$ on $L^2(G)$.

entry_2.statement: Under the transform, the regular action by shifts becomes multiplication by characters on the spectral side.

entry_1.statement: For $H \leq G$ with $G$ abelian, bi-$H$-invariant functions on $G$ form a commutative algebra under convolution, isomorphic via Fourier transform to functions on $H^\perp \subseteq \hat G$.

entry_2.statement: Signals constant on $H$-cosets are analyzed using only the frequency modes whose characters are trivial on $H$; convolution of such signals becomes multiplication on that restricted frequency set.

pairs.topic: Number theory: Dirichlet characters as Fourier modes

entry_1.statement: Dirichlet characters mod $n$ are the irreducible representations of $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$.

entry_2.statement: Fourier analysis on the finite unit group modulo $n$ uses the usual multiplicative residue-class homomorphisms as its frequency basis, so functions on that group expand in those modes.

entry_1.statement: The Schur function $s_\lambda(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ is the quotient of alternants $\det(x_i^{\lambda_j + n - j}) / \det(x_i^{n - j})$, equivalently the character of the irreducible polynomial representation of $GL_n$ indexed by $\lambda$.

entry_2.statement: The same symmetric function is obtained by listing all semistandard fillings of shape $\lambda$ with entries at most $n$ and recording each filling by the monomial determined by its content.

entry_1.statement: The dimension of the irreducible $S_n$-representation $S^\lambda$ indexed by $\lambda \vdash n$.

entry_2.statement: Equivalently, it is the number of standard fillings of the Young diagram of $\lambda$, computed by dividing $n!$ by the product of the hook lengths of all cells.

entry_1.statement: $\displaystyle\prod_{i,j}\dfrac{1}{1 - x_i y_j} = \sum_\lambda s_\lambda(x) s_\lambda(y)$ as a power-series identity in $\Lambda(x) \otimes \Lambda(y)$.

entry_2.statement: RSK sends a finite-support matrix of nonnegative integers to two semistandard tableaux sharing one shape, translating matrix margins into the two tableau contents.

entry_1.statement: $\displaystyle\sum_{\lambda \vdash n} (\dim S^\lambda)^2 = n!$.

entry_2.statement: RSK pairs each permutation with two standard tableaux having the same partition shape, so summing the squares of the shape counts recovers all permutations.

entry_1.statement: $s_\lambda = \det(h_{\lambda_i - i + j})_{1 \leq i, j \leq \ell(\lambda)}$, where $h_k$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric function.

entry_2.statement: Using the Lindstrom-Gessel-Viennot lemma, the weight enumerator for a nonintersecting family of lattice paths is computed as a determinant of the corresponding one-path enumerators.
